newsitem.title: USA: Tosco says Trainer plant testing before full ops.
newsitem.headline: Tosco says Trainer plant testing before full ops.

text.p: Tosco Corp has told local residents in Trainer, Pennsylvania and nearby towns that its 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery is being tested prior to full operation.
"We're almost ready to go," says Tosco in an information sheet distributed to the local population in Trainer, Marcus Hook and Linwood earlier this week.
The restart of the refinery has been closely watched since a battle with the Oil Chemical and Atomic Workers Union closed the refinery during the handover by BP Oil to Tosco in early 1996.
A subsequent agreement, which led to a sharp cutback in the workforce and a $110 million investment by Tosco in the plant, aimed to for an "early summer" 1997 restart.
The restart looks to be ahead of schedule.
The timing of the restart is of particular interest to traders in the Atlantic Basin gasoline market as the refinery is expected to add about 100,000 bpd of supply to that market.
"Our startup process will take about two weeks to complete," Tosco's information sheet said.
"The main refinery flare has been refurbished, lit and returned to service...Towers, drums and other vessels are being closed and readied for operation.
"...You may see steam coming from the top of the vessels along Post Road - this is a nomral part of our startup procedure. Pumps and other machinery are being tested prior to full operation."
Local environmental officials said they've been told the plant is expected to be fully operational before the end of the month.
